name: Emerald Energy
about:
Emerald Energy is a Raleigh, North Carolina-based solar installation and electrical contracting firm. The company is led by three co-owners: original owner Joey Wood, joined by John Leonard (President) and Justin Dunlap (Vice President). Leonard holds a business degree from North Carolina State University and brings over 20 years in the energy-saving industry, while Dunlap, also an NC State graduate, contributes engineering expertise and quality management experience. Wood, a graduate of Pitt Community College in electronic servicing, oversees field installations with a focus on detail and aesthetics.

The company provides design, consulting, and turnkey installation of solar photovoltaic systems for residential, commercial, and off-grid applications. Services extend to micro-grid solutions, energy storage, generator installation, EV charging stations, energy monitoring, and general electrical wiring. Emerald Energy manages the full project lifecycle, including permitting, HOA approvals, utility interconnection, and ongoing maintenance. The firm operates across the entire state of North Carolina, serving clients in cities such as Raleigh, Durham, Charlotte, and Asheville.

Emerald Energy’s customer base includes homeowners seeking energy independence and businesses aiming to reduce utility costs. Testimonials from residential clients in the Raleigh area highlight inverter replacements, system monitoring repairs, and new installations. The company also serves commercial properties, though specific project examples are not detailed in the available information.

The company positions itself as a partner in the transition to solar, emphasizing a manufacturer-agnostic approach that allows component selection based on client needs rather than supplier contracts. Its stated mission is to empower North Carolina residents and businesses to take control of their energy future, combining industry-leading technology with personalized service to deliver systems that maximize efficiency and savings.
